title: Unconditional exclusion of linear-time CNF satisfiability
formal: Is CNF satisfiability outside deterministic linear time on multitape Turing machines: does no deterministic machine decide every explicitly encoded CNF formula in \(O(L)\) time, where \(L\) is its full input bit length and no additional workspace restriction is imposed?
why: An unconditional lower bound for satisfiability would establish a limitation of general computation for a central natural problem, beyond limitations of a solver family or consequences of a conjecture. Even a modest bound is significant when it applies without an extra memory restriction. Its precise computational model is part of the mathematical achievement.

sentences: CNF satisfiability asks whether an assignment makes every listed clause true.
The input measure counts every written literal, identifier bit and delimiter.
The selected question asks whether a deterministic multitape Turing machine can always decide it in linear time.
No separate workspace restriction or conjectural hardness assumption is allowed.
This precise modest milestone is distinguished from exponential lower bounds and from lower bounds for other computation models.

definitions: A CNF formula is an AND of a finite list of clauses, each clause an OR of a finite list of signed variable occurrences. A variable takes a Boolean value; a positive occurrence is true at value 1 and a negative occurrence at value 0. Empty clauses are false and an empty conjunction is true. Clause width and the number of occurrences are unrestricted; repeated occurrences or clauses are allowed. The input alphabet is a fixed finite alphabet encoded by a fixed-length binary code. Each variable identifier is a nonempty canonical binary representation of a positive integer, preceded by a sign symbol; clause separators and an end marker delimit the full list. The complete explicit string, including every identifier bit, sign and separator, has length \(L\). Unused or nonconsecutive identifiers are allowed and denote no extra work beyond their written bits. There are no circuit or compressed-formula encodings. A deterministic multitape Turing machine has a fixed finite program, fixed finite tape alphabets and a fixed finite number of tapes with one head per tape. In one step it reads and writes a constant number of symbols and moves each head by at most one cell; it has no random access, word arithmetic instruction, advice, randomness or oracle. The input tape initially holds the encoding and other tapes are blank. Deciding SAT means halting with YES exactly when some assignment satisfies the formula. On malformed inputs it may reject. Linear time means that there are a correct machine and constants \(C,L_0\) such that every valid formula of length \(L\ge L_0\) is decided within \(CL\) steps. The claim negates the existence of such a machine and constants; it does not demand a fixed superlinear power or exponential variable dependence. Memory is unrestricted except for what can be visited within the elapsed time. An unconditional proof may not assume a complexity separation or a fine-grained hardness hypothesis.
answer_criterion: Provide an unconditional Lean proof that no machine has the stated linear worst-case bound, or a Lean-certified deterministic linear-time SAT algorithm in the stated encoding and machine model. A lower bound requiring an additional workspace bound, a conditional lower bound, or hardness of a different language does not meet this criterion.
